prompt: On most rural interstate highways in New Mexico, the maximum posted speed limit for passenger vehicles is:
explanation: New Mexico posts a maximum of 75 mph on most rural interstate highways. You must still slow to a safe speed for traffic, weather, and road conditions.

references.label: NM Driver Manual
references.citation: NM MVD Driver Manual, Speed Limits

prompt: You are driving through a marked school zone in New Mexico during posted hours. Unless another limit is posted, you should not exceed:
explanation: New Mexico school zones are commonly posted at 15 mph during the hours shown on the sign. Always obey the posted limit and watch for children.

references.label: NM Driver Manual
references.citation: NM MVD Driver Manual, School Zones

prompt: In New Mexico, a driver age 21 or older is legally impaired (per se) at a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
explanation: For drivers 21 and older, 0.08% BAC is the per se limit in New Mexico. Commercial drivers are limited to 0.04%.

references.label: NM Driver Manual
references.citation: NM MVD Driver Manual, Alcohol and the Law

prompt: Under New Mexico's zero tolerance law, a driver under 21 can be charged for driving with a BAC as low as:
explanation: New Mexico's zero tolerance law makes it illegal for a driver under 21 to drive with a BAC of 0.02% or higher.

references.label: NM Driver Manual
references.citation: NM MVD Driver Manual, Underage Drinking and Driving

prompt: Before a New Mexico teen can move from an instruction permit to a provisional license, they must hold the permit for at least:
explanation: New Mexico requires holding the instruction permit for at least 6 months, with 50 hours of supervised driving (10 at night), before applying for a provisional license.

references.label: NM Driver Manual
references.citation: NM MVD Driver Manual, Graduated Licensing

prompt: A New Mexico provisional license holder is generally restricted from driving during which hours (unless an exception applies)?
explanation: Provisional drivers in New Mexico generally may not drive between midnight and 5 a.m. and may carry no more than one passenger under 21, unless a listed exception applies.

references.label: NM Driver Manual
references.citation: NM MVD Driver Manual, Provisional License Restrictions

prompt: In New Mexico's driver point system, accumulating how many points within a 12-month period results in a one-year license suspension?
explanation: In New Mexico, 12 points in a 12-month period leads to a one-year suspension. Reaching 7 points can trigger a hearing that may result in a shorter suspension.

references.label: NM Driver Manual
references.citation: NM MVD Driver Manual, Point System

prompt: Under New Mexico's Move Over Law, when you approach a stopped emergency or highway maintenance vehicle with flashing lights on a multi-lane road, you must:
options: Speed up to clear the area quickly
Move over one lane if you safely can, or slow down
Stop completely until the vehicle leaves
Sound your horn and continue at the same speed
explanation: New Mexico's Move Over Law requires drivers to move over a lane when safe, or slow down, for stopped emergency, police, and highway maintenance vehicles displaying flashing lights.

references.label: NM Driver Manual
references.citation: NM MVD Driver Manual, Move Over Law

prompt: New Mexico's statewide distracted driving law prohibits which of the following for all drivers?
options: Reading or sending text messages while driving
explanation: New Mexico bans texting (reading or sending messages) while driving statewide. Some cities add stricter handheld-phone bans.

references.label: NM Driver Manual
references.citation: NM MVD Driver Manual, Distracted Driving

prompt: You reach a four-way stop at the same time as a vehicle on your right. Who has the right-of-way?
options: You do, because you are on the left
explanation: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

prompt: A yellow diamond-shaped sign in New Mexico is used to:
options: Give a regulatory order you must obey
Warn you of a hazard or change in conditions ahead
explanation: Yellow diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to hazards or changes ahead such as curves, intersections, or merging traffic.

references.label: NM Driver Manual
references.citation: NM MVD Driver Manual, Traffic Signs

prompt: A flashing red traffic signal means you must:
options: Slow down and proceed with caution
Stop, then proceed when it is safe, as at a stop sign
Stop and wait for the light to turn green
explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: come to a full stop, then proceed when it is safe to do so.

references.label: NM Driver Manual
references.citation: NM MVD Driver Manual, Traffic Signals

prompt: New Mexico includes wide-open desert and mountain highways. To reduce the danger of hitting wildlife or livestock, you should:
options: Use high beams at all times, even with oncoming traffic
Scan the road edges and reduce speed at dawn, dusk, and in open-range areas
Assume animals will move out of the way
Speed up to pass animals quickly
explanation: Animals are most active at dawn and dusk and may enter open-range roadways. Scanning the roadsides and slowing down gives you time to react safely.

references.label: NM Driver Manual
references.citation: NM MVD Driver Manual, Safe Driving Tips

prompt: When passing a bicyclist on a New Mexico roadway, you should:
options: Pass as closely as possible to save time
Give a safe distance and pass only when it is clear
Honk continuously until the cyclist moves off the road
explanation: Treat bicyclists as legal road users. Give them a safe passing distance and wait for a clear, safe opportunity to pass.

references.label: NM Driver Manual
references.citation: NM MVD Driver Manual, Sharing the Road
